name: Point-Sampled Spectrum Model
definition: A discrete spectral representation method where the spectrum is divided into N uniform bands by point-sampling at uniform intervals. It is used to approximate spectral distribution functions for volume rendering but suffers from energy conservation loss, information loss during Doppler shifts, and accuracy issues.
summary: The Point-Sampled Spectrum Model is a discrete spectral representation method for volume rendering that approximates spectral distributions by dividing the spectrum into uniform bands, specifically supporting the Doppler effect.
